description: One calibrated fire history from two satellites: a calendar that shows when a place normally burns and when it burns unusually
summary:
The Harmonized Burning Activity Index is an interactive platform designed to create a consistent historical record of satellite-detected burning activity by harmonizing NASA's MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations.

The project focuses on Punjab, India, where differences in satellite resolution, detection sensitivity and observation characteristics can make historical fire activity difficult to compare. We process MODIS Terra/Aqua Collection 6.1 and VIIRS S-NPP Collection 2 data from NASA FIRMS, aggregate detections into a common spatial grid, and calibrate the two sensors using their overlapping observation period (2013–2025).

The resulting harmonized index provides an interactive burning-activity calendar, historical comparisons, anomaly detection, and sensor calibration analysis. It helps researchers, environmental analysts and emergency-response planners identify seasonal patterns and unusually high or low burning activity.

Our goal is to transform incompatible satellite observations into a transparent, interpretable and scientifically validated historical activity record.
details:
Overview

The Harmonized Burning Activity Index is a data-driven web application developed to address the challenge of comparing historical active-fire observations from two different satellite instruments: MODIS and VIIRS.

Although both instruments detect active fires and thermal anomalies, their different spatial resolutions and detection characteristics produce significantly different observation counts. Directly combining their raw records can introduce artificial changes into historical fire trends.

Our solution creates a unified burning-activity record for Punjab, India, covering the geographical region between approximately 29.2°–32.1° N latitude and 73.5°–76.5° E longitude.

How It Works

The application follows a seven-stage processing pipeline:

  1. Data Collection: Retrieves historical MODIS Terra/Aqua Collection 6.1 and VIIRS S-NPP Collection 2 active-fire observations from NASA FIRMS.
  2. Data Cleaning: Processes observation timestamps, coordinates, confidence values and satellite information while filtering unsuitable detections.
  3. Spatial Harmonization: Maps observations onto a common 0.01° latitude-longitude grid, approximately 1 km in scale.
  4. Duplicate Removal: Counts each unique grid cell only once per day across the satellite observations.
  5. Monthly Aggregation: Aggregates daily unique active grid-cell observations into monthly activity values, expressed as cell-days.
  6. Sensor Calibration: Calculates calendar-month-specific median VIIRS/MODIS calibration ratios using overlapping observations from January 2013 to December 2025.
  7. Anomaly Detection: Compares monthly activity against historical observations for the same calendar month from 2003 to 2025 using percentiles and Z-scores.

Application Features

The Streamlit dashboard provides:

  • Overview: Key performance indicators, sensor comparison and historical activity trends.
  • Burning Calendar: A year-by-month heatmap showing historical burning activity.
  • Anomaly Analysis: Identifies unusually high or low activity compared with historical seasonal patterns.
  • Calibration Analysis: Displays sensor calibration ratios, uncertainty and temporal consistency.
  • Validation: Evaluates the harmonized record through correlation, relative bias, RMSE and comparison plots.
  • Methodology: Explains data processing, assumptions, limitations and calibration decisions.

Validation Results

The implemented application reports:

  • Held-out correlation: 0.983
  • Relative bias: 0.3%
  • Median VIIRS/MODIS calibration ratio: 4.59
  • Calibration period: January 2013 – December 2025

These results provide quantitative evidence of the agreement between the calibrated observations and the validation data.

Technology Stack

Programming Language: Python

Libraries: Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn and Plotly.

Application Framework: Streamlit.

Data Source: NASA Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS).

Innovation and Impact

The key innovation is transforming two fundamentally different satellite observation records into a common, calibrated historical activity index instead of simply combining their raw detection counts.

The application makes historical satellite fire observations easier to interpret through interactive visualizations, seasonal comparisons and anomaly indicators.

It can support environmental research, agricultural burning analysis, historical fire-pattern assessment and preliminary situational awareness for environmental monitoring and emergency-response planning.

Limitations

The index represents satellite-detected active-fire activity, not the actual number of fires or burned area on the ground. Cloud cover, smoke, satellite observation timing and detection sensitivity can affect observations.

Calibration ratios also vary by calendar month and should not be interpreted as universal sensor conversion factors.
